items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: I was on the road with Natalie Cole with the “Unforgettable” album... packing up the scores of Johnny Mandel... Johnny Mandel there were three voicings like this... that’s when I did my first charts.

ctx.x: I do. And I’m wondering how you learned to write for strings? Because I’ve done a bit of it and I know enough to know that I don’t know much about what they’re capable of.

Yeah well that’s what happened to me. I really didn’t have a clue. Because I was a pianist with Nelson Riddle for the last ten years of his life. I was there when he didn’t — this was way past Sinatra and stuff, but he did TV shows and things. But I never asked him, I never, he was always kind of austere. A lovely guy and kind to me, but he wasn’t interested in teaching in that way. So I would listen. And then eventually I got to be on the road with Natalie Cole with the “Unforgettable” album and, as her pianist.…

mean all these guys, and there they were. So that’s what I did on the bus, on the luxury bus where you felt every bump no matter how — but I had the time. And there — “Oh you mean you do that with the violins and then the violas can —” it was spelled out for me. And I suddenly could, all I thought I knew about the orchestra was my years of watching — I mean looking at scores since I was a teenager. Huge collection which I still have. They didn’t teach me anything. But Johnny Mandel there were three voicings like…
